note: Parks no keyword can see. site/src/lib/parks.ts derives the park a tree stands in from its address text matching a word list, which is the right mechanism for the thousands of Parks, Jardins, Giardini and Plantsoenen and cannot work for a place whose name says nothing about being one. Written 2026-09-19, after the fifth such place turned up in a week: Margaret Island in Budapest holds five of our trees whose addresses all begin 'Margaret Island', and no word that would catch it is safe to add, because 'island' is a substring of Islandbridge and 'mall' of Smallbrook Street.
how_it_matches: EXACT, case-insensitive, on the head clause the address or neighbourhood already produces, and only when NEITHER field yields a keyword match. Exact rather than substring because the near misses are real: 'Pfaueninsel ferry landing' is not the Pfaueninsel and 'Kalopanagiotis village' in Cyprus is not Hawaii's Kalopa. Last rather than first because a keyword match is more specific: a Montjuic tree whose address names the Jardi Botanic Historic belongs to that garden, not to the hill, and this list must never move a tree out of a group it already has.
the_bar: A name goes in only when the place is genuinely a park, garden or protected landscape somebody spends an afternoon in. Neighbourhoods stay out, and they are the overwhelming majority of what the keyword list misses: City centre, Binnenstad, Santa Cruz, Mokotow, Norrebro, Dahlem. A district is not a park, and a park page wearing a district's name would be the thin page Contract H's five-tree gate exists to prevent.

Montjuic.why: the Parc de Montjuic, a hill of public gardens above the city

Kalopa State Recreation Area.why: a state park on Hamakua, native forest with a trail system

Margaret Island.why: Margitsziget, a public park island in the Danube

La Granja de San Ildefonso.why: the royal palace gardens, UNESCO listed, open to visitors

Pfaueninsel.why: a UNESCO listed park island in the Havel, reached by ferry

Alhambra.why: the Alhambra and Generalife gardens, UNESCO listed

Kyoto Gyoen.why: the national garden around the imperial palace, free and open daily

Square Louise Michel.why: the public garden below Sacre-Coeur on Montmartre

National Mall.why: the Mall itself, whose American elms are a documented collection
